claim: Rice Pik-1 comprises an integrated heavy metal-associated (HMA) domain.
source: One example is rice Pik-1 that comprises an integrated heavy metal-associated (HMA) domain.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of Pik-1.

claim: The HMA domain integrated into Pik-1 before Oryzinae speciation over 15 million years ago.
source: Phylogenetic analyses revealed that the HMA domain integrated into Pik-1 before Oryzinae speciation over 15 million years ago and has been under diversifying selection.
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: The HMA domain of Pik-1 has been under diversifying selection.
source: Phylogenetic analyses revealed that the HMA domain integrated into Pik-1 before Oryzinae speciation over 15 million years ago and has been under diversifying selection.
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analyses and selection tests presented in the manuscript.

claim: Two Pik-1 allelic variants independently evolved from a weakly binding ancestral state to high-affinity binding of the blast fungus effector AVR-PikD.
source: Ancestral sequence reconstruction coupled with functional studies showed that two Pik-1 allelic variants independently evolved from a weakly binding ancestral state to high-affinity binding of the blast fungus effector AVR-PikD.
evidence: Based on ancestral sequence reconstruction and functional binding studies.

claim: For most of its evolutionary history the Pik-1 HMA domain did not sense AVR-PikD.
source: We conclude that for most of its evolutionary history the Pik-1 HMA domain did not sense AVR-PikD, and that different Pik-1 receptors have recently evolved through distinct biochemical paths to produce similar phenotypic outcomes.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from ancestral sequence reconstruction and binding studies showing weak ancestral binding.

claim: Different Pik-1 receptors have recently evolved through distinct biochemical paths to produce similar phenotypic outcomes.
source: We conclude that for most of its evolutionary history the Pik-1 HMA domain did not sense AVR-PikD, and that different Pik-1 receptors have recently evolved through distinct biochemical paths to produce similar phenotypic outcomes.
evidence: Based on analysis of different evolutionary paths in Pikp-1 and Pikm-1 leading to AVR-PikD binding.

claim: NLR proteins constitute an ancient class of intracellular immune receptors that confer innate immunity in plants and animals.
source: Nucleotide-binding domain leucine-rich repeat–containing (NLR) proteins constitute an ancient class of intracellular immune receptors that confer innate immunity in plants and animals (Dodds and Rathjen, 2010; Jones et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: In plants, NLRs function by sensing pathogen-derived virulence molecules, known as effectors, and subsequently activating an immune response.
source: In plants, NLRs function by sensing pathogen-derived virulence molecules, known as effectors, and subsequently activating an immune response (Jacob et al., 2013; Kourelis and van der Hoorn, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The majority of functionally validated NLRs in plants display broadly conserved domain architectures, typically consisting of the NB-ARC domain, the LRR region, and either a TIR, CC, or CCR domain at the N-terminus.
source: The majority of functionally validated NLRs in plants display broadly conserved domain architectures, typically consisting of the NB-ARC (nucleotide-binding adaptor shared by APAF-1, certain R gene products and CED-4) domain, the LRR (leucin-rich repeat) region, and either a TIR (Toll/interleukin 1 receptor), CC (coiled-coil), or CCR (RPW8-type CC) domain at the N-terminus (Kourelis and Kamoun, 2020; Shao et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Coevolution with pathogen effectors has led to a remarkable diversification of NLR repertoires, which form one of the most diverse protein families in plants.
source: However, coevolution with pathogen effectors has led to a remarkable diversification of NLR repertoires, which form one of the most diverse protein families in plants (Lee and Chae, 2020; Prigozhin and Krasileva, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Some NLRs acquired novel recognition specificities through fusions of noncanonical integrated domains (IDs) that mediate perception of effectors.
source: An emerging paradigm in plant immunity is that some NLRs acquired novel recognition specificities through fusions of noncanonical integrated domains (IDs) that mediate perception of effectors (Cesari et al., 2014a; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: NLR-IDs have been described across various plant families.
source: Although NLR-IDs have been described across various plant families (Gao et al., 2018; Kroj et al., 2016; Sarris et al., 2016; Van de Weyer et al., 2019), little is known about their emergence and subsequent evolution.
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Little is known about the emergence and subsequent evolution of NLR-IDs.
source: Although NLR-IDs have been described across various plant families (Gao et al., 2018; Kroj et al., 2016; Sarris et al., 2016; Van de Weyer et al., 2019), little is known about their emergence and subsequent evolution.
evidence: Statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: IDs are generally thought to have derived from effector operative targets, which then act as baits for effector recognition within NLRs.
source: Given that many IDs exhibit homology to molecules required for immune responses, they are generally thought to have derived from effector operative targets, which then act as baits for effector recognition within NLRs (Cesari et al., 2014a; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: IDs can perceive effectors by direct binding, by serving as substrates for their enzymatic activities, or by detecting effector-induced perturbations.
source: IDs can perceive effectors by direct binding, by serving as substrates for their enzymatic activities, or by detecting effector-induced perturbations (Bao et al., 2017; Cesari et al., 2014a; Fujisaki et al., 2017; Heidrich et al., 2013; Sarris et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: RGA5 and Pik-1 detect three unrelated effectors from the rice blast fungus, Magnaporthe oryzae, AVR-Pia/AVR1-CO39 and AVR-Pik, respectively, via their integrated heavy metal-associated (HMA) domains.
source: The RGA5 (also known as Pia-2) and Pik-1 receptors are well-characterised examples of NLR-IDs. RGA5 and Pik-1 detect three unrelated effectors from the rice blast fungus, Magnaporthe oryzae, AVR-Pia/AVR1-CO39 and AVR-Pik, respectively, via their integrated heavy metal-associated (HMA) domains (De la Concepcion et al., 2018; Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: HMAs are commonly found in a family of HMA plant proteins (HPPs) or HMA isoprenylated plant proteins (HIPPs) known to contribute to abiotic and biotic stress responses.
source: HMAs are commonly found in a family of HMA plant proteins (HPPs) or HMA isoprenylated plant proteins (HIPPs) known to contribute to abiotic and biotic stress responses (de Abreu-Neto et al., 2013; Fukuoka et al., 2009; Li et al., 2020a; Radakovic et al., 2018; Zschiesche et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: AVR-Pik effectors bind and stabilise rice HMA proteins to co-opt their function in immunity.
source: Recently, the AVR-Pik effectors have been shown to bind and stabilise rice HMA proteins to co-opt their function in immunity (Maidment et al., 2020; Oikawa et al., 2020), providing direct evidence that integrated HMAs indeed mimic host targets of effectors.
evidence: Supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Integrated HMAs mimic host targets of effectors.
source: Recently, the AVR-Pik effectors have been shown to bind and stabilise rice HMA proteins to co-opt their function in immunity (Maidment et al., 2020; Oikawa et al., 2020), providing direct evidence that integrated HMAs indeed mimic host targets of effectors.
evidence: Inference drawn from cited studies showing AVR-Pik binding to HMA proteins.

claim: NLR-triggered immunity is usually accompanied by the hypersensitive response (HR), a type of localised cell death associated with disease resistance.
source: NLR-triggered immunity is usually accompanied by the hypersensitive response (HR), a type of localised cell death associated with disease resistance.
evidence: Statement of established knowledge in plant immunity.

claim: Several NLR-IDs appear to have lost the ability to autonomously trigger a defence response.
source: Notably, several NLR-IDs appear to have lost the ability to autonomously trigger a defence response (Cesari et al., 2014b; Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: NLR-IDs often function in pairs, where the NLR-ID serves as a sensor for pathogen effectors and its partner acts as a helper that mediates activation of an immune response.
source: As a consequence, they often function in pairs, where the NLR-ID serves as a sensor for pathogen effectors and its partner acts as a helper that mediates activation of an immune response (Adachi et al., 2019; Bonardi et al., 2011; Feehan et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Many NLR pairs are encoded by two adjacent genes in a head-to-head orientation.
source: Many NLR pairs are encoded by two adjacent genes in a head-to-head orientation (Bailey et al., 2018; Van de Weyer et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Genetic linkage of NLR pairs likely provides an evolutionary advantage by facilitating co-segregation, coevolution, and transcriptional coregulation of functionally linked genes.
source: This genetic linkage likely provides an evolutionary advantage by facilitating co-segregation, coevolution, and transcriptional coregulation of functionally linked genes (Baggs et al., 2017; Griebel et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Genetic linkage may reduce the genetic load caused by autoimmunity.
source: Genetic linkage may also reduce the genetic load caused by autoimmunity (Wu et al., 2018), which is a common phenomenon observed across NLRs (Alcázar et al., 2009; Bomblies et al., 2007; Chae et al., 2016; Deng et al., 2019; Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Autoimmunity is a common phenomenon observed across NLRs.
source: Genetic linkage may also reduce the genetic load caused by autoimmunity (Wu et al., 2018), which is a common phenomenon observed across NLRs (Alcázar et al., 2009; Bomblies et al., 2007; Chae et al., 2016; Deng et al., 2019; Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Rice Pik-1 and Pik-2 proteins form a CC-type NLR pair.
source: Rice Pik-1 and Pik-2 proteins form a CC-type NLR pair.
evidence: Statement of established knowledge about Pik proteins.

claim: Two Pik haplotypes, N- and K-type, are present in the genetic pool of wild and cultivated rice.
source: Two Pik haplotypes, N- and K-type, are present in the genetic pool of wild and cultivated rice (Zhai et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to established literature.

claim: K-type Pik NLRs confer resistance to the rice blast fungus.
source: While the function of the N-type haplotypes remains obscure, K-type Pik NLRs confer resistance to the rice blast fungus.
evidence: Statement of established knowledge about K-type Pik function.

claim: In the K-type pair, Pik-1 acts as a sensor that binds the AVR-Pik effector via the Pik-1-integrated HMA domain.
source: In the K-type pair, Pik-1 acts as a sensor that binds the AVR-Pik effector via the Pik-1-integrated HMA domain, whereas Pik-2 is required for activation of immune response upon effector recognition (Maqbool et al., 2015; Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Pik-2 is required for activation of immune response upon effector recognition.
source: In the K-type pair, Pik-1 acts as a sensor that binds the AVR-Pik effector via the Pik-1-integrated HMA domain, whereas Pik-2 is required for activation of immune response upon effector recognition (Maqbool et al., 2015; Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The Pik NLR pair was initially cloned from Tsuyuake rice.
source: This NLR pair was initially cloned from Tsuyuake rice (Ashikawa et al., 2008) and has since been shown to occur in allelic variants, which include Pikp, Pikm, Piks, Pikh, and Pik* (Costanzo and Jia, 2010; Jia et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009; Yuan et al., 2011; Zhai et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to established literature.

claim: The Pik NLR pair occurs in allelic variants, which include Pikp, Pikm, Piks, Pikh, and Pik*.
source: This NLR pair was initially cloned from Tsuyuake rice (Ashikawa et al., 2008) and has since been shown to occur in allelic variants, which include Pikp, Pikm, Piks, Pikh, and Pik* (Costanzo and Jia, 2010; Jia et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009; Yuan et al., 2011; Zhai et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The integrated HMA domain is the most sequence-diverse region among Pik-1 variants.
source: Remarkably, the integrated HMA domain is the most sequence-diverse region among Pik-1 variants, consistent with the view that the receptor is under selection imposed by AVR-Pik (Białas et al., 2018; Costanzo and Jia, 2010; De la Concepcion et al., 2021; Zhai et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The Pik-1 receptor is under selection imposed by AVR-Pik.
source: Remarkably, the integrated HMA domain is the most sequence-diverse region among Pik-1 variants, consistent with the view that the receptor is under selection imposed by AVR-Pik (Białas et al., 2018; Costanzo and Jia, 2010; De la Concepcion et al., 2021; Zhai et al., 2014).
evidence: Inference supported by citations and sequence diversity data.

claim: AVR-Pik alleles carry only five amino acid replacements, all of which map to regions located at the HMA-binding interface.
source: Conversely, AVR-Pik alleles carry only five amino acid replacements, all of which map to regions located at the HMA-binding interface, indicating the adaptive nature of those polymorphisms (Longya et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to established literature.

claim: The polymorphisms in AVR-Pik alleles are adaptive in nature.
source: Conversely, AVR-Pik alleles carry only five amino acid replacements, all of which map to regions located at the HMA-binding interface, indicating the adaptive nature of those polymorphisms (Longya et al., 2019).
evidence: Inference supported by citation and the location of polymorphisms at binding interface.

claim: AVR-PikD is the most ancient of the AVR-Pik allelic variants.
source: While the most ancient of the AVR-Pik allelic variants, AVR-PikD, is recognised by a wide range of Pik-1 proteins, the most recent variants, AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF, evade recognition by all known Pik-1 variants (Kanzaki et al., 2012; Longya et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: AVR-PikD is recognised by a wide range of Pik-1 proteins.
source: While the most ancient of the AVR-Pik allelic variants, AVR-PikD, is recognised by a wide range of Pik-1 proteins, the most recent variants, AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF, evade recognition by all known Pik-1 variants (Kanzaki et al., 2012; Longya et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF evade recognition by all known Pik-1 variants.
source: While the most ancient of the AVR-Pik allelic variants, AVR-PikD, is recognised by a wide range of Pik-1 proteins, the most recent variants, AVR-PikC and AVR-PikF, evade recognition by all known Pik-1 variants (Kanzaki et al., 2012; Longya et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Recognition specificities of AVR-Pik variants reflect the ongoing arms race between rice and the rice blast fungus.
source: These recognition specificities are thought to reflect the ongoing arms race between rice and the rice blast fungus (Białas et al., 2018; Kanzaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2019) and have been linked to the effector–HMA binding affinity (De la Concepcion et al., 2021; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; Maqbool et al., 2015).
evidence: Inference supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Recognition specificities have been linked to the effector–HMA binding affinity.
source: These recognition specificities are thought to reflect the ongoing arms race between rice and the rice blast fungus (Białas et al., 2018; Kanzaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2019) and have been linked to the effector–HMA binding affinity (De la Concepcion et al., 2021; De la Concepcion et al., 2018; Maqbool et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Pik-1 and Pik-2 sequences fell into two phylogenetically unrelated, but well-supported, clades.
source: Next, we constructed a maximum likelihood (ML) phylogenetic tree based on protein sequences of the NB-ARC domain of recovered CC-NLRs and discovered that the Pik-1 and Pik-2 sequences fell into two phylogenetically unrelated, but well-supported, clades (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pik-1 and Pik-2 orthologues were detected in representatives from different, often distantly related, grass species, including members of the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies.
source: Among Pik-1- and Pik-2-related sequences, we detected representatives from different, often distantly related, grass species, including members of the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies.
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis and sequence identification.

claim: Pik-2 from Oryza brachyantha was N-terminally truncated as a result of a 46 bp deletion within its 5′-region.
source: We noted that Pik-2 from Oryza brachyantha was N-terminally truncated as a result of a 46 bp deletion within its 5′-region (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Full-length ObPik-2 genes without the deletion are present in the O. brachyantha population.
source: To determine whether the O. brachyantha population carries a full-length Pik-2 gene, we genotyped 16 additional O. brachyantha accessions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B). We successfully amplified and sequenced six full-length ObPik-2 genes, none of which carried the deletion present in the reference genome.
evidence: Based on genotyping data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The majority of species within the Oryzinae subtribe contain single copies of Pik-1 and Pik-2 per accession.
source: The majority of species within the Oryzinae subtribe contain single copies of Pik-1 and Pik-2 per accession, whereas members of the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies frequently encode multiple Pik-1 or Pik-2 paralogues, with wheat carrying as many as 9 and 10 Pik-1 and Pik-2 genes, respectively.
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis and gene identification across species.

claim: Members of the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies frequently encode multiple Pik-1 or Pik-2 paralogues.
source: The majority of species within the Oryzinae subtribe contain single copies of Pik-1 and Pik-2 per accession, whereas members of the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies frequently encode multiple Pik-1 or Pik-2 paralogues, with wheat carrying as many as 9 and 10 Pik-1 and Pik-2 genes, respectively.
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis and gene identification across species.

claim: Wheat carries as many as 9 and 10 Pik-1 and Pik-2 genes, respectively.
source: The majority of species within the Oryzinae subtribe contain single copies of Pik-1 and Pik-2 per accession, whereas members of the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies frequently encode multiple Pik-1 or Pik-2 paralogues, with wheat carrying as many as 9 and 10 Pik-1 and Pik-2 genes, respectively.
evidence: Based on gene identification in wheat genome.

claim: Pik-1 and Pik-2 from the Oryza genus formed two subclades, corresponding to the two haplotypes previously identified at the Pik locus, N-type and K-type.
source: In addition, Pik-1 and Pik-2 from the Oryza genus formed two subclades, corresponding to the two haplotypes previously identified at the Pik locus, N-type and K-type (Figure 1—figure supplement 3; Zhai et al., 2011).
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and cited literature.

claim: The N- and K-type Pik genes have been maintained through speciation and coexist as haplotypes in different Oryza species.
source: We conclude that the N- and K-type Pik genes have been maintained through speciation and coexist as haplotypes in different Oryza species.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Pik-1 and Pik-2 orthologues are present across a wide range of grasses, including members of the Oryzoideae, Pooideae, and Panicoideae subfamilies.
source: Altogether, we discovered that Pik-1 and Pik-2 orthologues are present across a wide range of grasses, including members of the Oryzoideae, Pooideae, and Panicoideae subfamilies.
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis and gene identification across grass species.

claim: A total of 14 out of 15 species in which both Pik-1 and Pik-2 genes are present carry at least one Pik pair with adjacent Pik-1 and Pik-2 genes in a head-to-head orientation.
source: A total of 14 out of 15 species in which both genes are present carry at least one Pik pair with adjacent Pik-1 and Pik-2 genes in a head-to-head orientation.
evidence: Based on examination of genetic loci across species.

claim: The length of the Pik genes and their intergenic regions vary between species (from ~2 kb in O. nivara to ~48 Mb in wheat).
source: Although the length of the genes and their intergenic regions vary between species (from ~2 kb in O. nivara to ~48 Mb in wheat), they exhibit largely conserved gene models.
evidence: Based on examination of genetic loci across species.

claim: Pik genes exhibit largely conserved gene models across species.
source: Although the length of the genes and their intergenic regions vary between species (from ~2 kb in O. nivara to ~48 Mb in wheat), they exhibit largely conserved gene models.
evidence: Based on examination of genetic loci across species.

claim: Most of the Pik-2 orthologues feature one intron in their nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) region.
source: Most of the Pik-2 orthologues feature one intron in their nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) region (Ashikawa et al., 2008) while the Pik-1 genes typically carry one or, for the genes featuring the HMA domain, two introns (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1F).
evidence: Based on gene structure analysis shown in Figure 1B and cited literature.

claim: Pik-1 genes typically carry one or, for the genes featuring the HMA domain, two introns.
source: Most of the Pik-2 orthologues feature one intron in their nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) region (Ashikawa et al., 2008) while the Pik-1 genes typically carry one or, for the genes featuring the HMA domain, two introns (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1F).
evidence: Based on gene structure analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There is strong positive correlation of dS rates (R2 = 0.87, p-value=0.95) between genetically linked Pik genes.
source: The comparisons revealed strong positive correlation of dS rates (R2 = 0.87, p-value=0.95) between genetically linked Pik genes (Figure 1C).
evidence: Based on dS rate analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The correlation of dS rates between genetically linked Pik genes was significantly higher than observed by chance.
source: This was significantly higher than observed by chance, as calculated from random Pik-1–Pik-2 cross-referencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Based on statistical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The Pik-1/Pik-2 pair probably became genetically linked long before the emergence of the Oryzinae clade and prior to the split of the major grass lineages—the BOP and PACMAD clades—which dates back to 100–50 MYA.
source: We conclude that the Pik-1/Pik-2 pair probably became genetically linked long before the emergence of the Oryzinae clade and prior to the split of the major grass lineages—the BOP (for Bambusoideae, Oryzoideae, Pooideae) and PACMAD (for Panicoideae, Arundinoideae, Chloridoideae, Micrairoideae, Aristidoideae, Danthonioideae) clades—which dates back to 100–50 MYA (Hodkinson, 2018).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from dS rate correlation analysis and cited dating of grass lineage splits.

claim: HMA-containing Pik-1 clustered into a single well-supported clade (the Pik-1 integration clade).
source: Remarkably, the presence of an HMA domain varied among Pik-1 genes. HMA-containing Pik-1 clustered into a single well-supported clade (herein called the Pik-1 integration clade) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Based on phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: All members of the Pik-1 integration clade carry the HMA domain in the same position, between the CC and NB-ARC domains of Pik-1, and feature an intron within the HMA.
source: All members of the Pik-1 integration clade carry the HMA domain in the same position, between the CC and NB-ARC domains of Pik-1, and feature an intron within the HMA (Figure 1B).
evidence: Based on gene structure analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The HMA domains in the Pik-1 integration clade are likely derived from a single integration event.
source: This implies that these HMA domains are likely derived from a single integration event.
evidence: Inference drawn from phylogenetic clustering and conserved position of HMA domain.

claim: All Oryza Pik-1 orthologues carry the HMA domain.
source: We found that all Oryza Pik-1 orthologues carry the HMA domain, which indicates that the integration predates speciation of this genus.
evidence: Based on examination of Pik-1 sequences from Oryza species.

claim: The HMA integration predates speciation of the Oryza genus.
source: We found that all Oryza Pik-1 orthologues carry the HMA domain, which indicates that the integration predates speciation of this genus.
evidence: Inference drawn from presence of HMA in all Oryza Pik-1 orthologues.

claim: The HMA fusion probably occurred before the speciation of Oryzinae, dated at ~15 MYA.
source: Although we failed to detect a full-length HMA integration in L. perrieri, LpPik-1 carries ~15 amino acids characteristic of the HMA integration site (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that the fusion probably occurred before the speciation of Oryzinae, dated at ~15 MYA (Jacquemin et al., 2011), and was subsequently lost in L. perrieri.
evidence: Inference drawn from partial HMA sequence in L. perrieri and cited dating of Oryzinae speciation.

claim: The HMA integration was subsequently lost in L. perrieri.
source: Although we failed to detect a full-length HMA integration in L. perrieri, LpPik-1 carries ~15 amino acids characteristic of the HMA integration site (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that the fusion probably occurred before the speciation of Oryzinae, dated at ~15 MYA (Jacquemin et al., 2011), and was subsequently lost in L. perrieri.
evidence: Inference drawn from partial HMA sequence in L. perrieri.

claim: The vast majority of examined Pik-1 from the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies lack the HMA domain.
source: By contrast, the vast majority of examined Pik-1 from the Pooideae and Panicoideae subfamilies lack the HMA domain.
evidence: Based on examination of Pik-1 sequences from these subfamilies.

claim: One of the nine Pik-1 paralogues of wheat carries an HMA integration.
source: The only integration in these taxonomic groups was detected in one of the nine Pik-1 paralogues of wheat included in the analysis.
evidence: Based on examination of wheat Pik-1 sequences.

claim: dN was greater than dS in 96 out of 115 pairwise sequence comparisons of the HMA domain (86/105 for K- and 10/10 for N-type HMAs; ω = dN/dS ranging 0–2.45 for K-type and 1.13–3.50 for N-type).
source: We discovered that dN was greater than dS in 96 out of 115 pairwise sequence comparisons (86/105 for K- and 10/10 for N-type HMAs; ω = dN/dS ranging 0–2.45 for K-type and 1.13–3.50 for N-type) (Figure 2A–C), providing evidence that positive selection has acted on the integrated HMA domain.
evidence: Based on dN/dS analysis shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Positive selection has acted on the integrated HMA domain.
source: We discovered that dN was greater than dS in 96 out of 115 pairwise sequence comparisons (86/105 for K- and 10/10 for N-type HMAs; ω = dN/dS ranging 0–2.45 for K-type and 1.13–3.50 for N-type) (Figure 2A–C), providing evidence that positive selection has acted on the integrated HMA domain.
evidence: Inference drawn from dN/dS ratios greater than 1.

claim: Only 9 out of 115 pairs of the NB-ARC domain sequences displayed dN greater than dS.
source: By contrast, only 9 out of 115 pairs of the NB-ARC domain sequences of the same set of genes displayed dN greater than dS (Figure 2B–D); however, all of these showed dS = 0 and were therefore inconclusive in calculating ω (dN/dS) ratios.
evidence: Based on dN/dS analysis shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: The integrated HMA domain exhibits marked signatures of positive selection in contrast to the Pik-1 NB-ARC domain.
source: Overall, these results demonstrate that the integrated HMA domain exhibits marked signatures of positive selection in contrast to the Pik-1 NB-ARC domain.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparison of dN/dS ratios between HMA and NB-ARC domains.

claim: Approximately 26% of the HMA amino acid sites likely experienced positive selection.
source: As indicated by the likelihood ratio tests (LRTs) and posterior probabilities, ~26% of the HMA amino acid sites likely experienced positive selection (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B, C; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Based on ML codon substitution model analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B, C.

claim: The ancHMA variants exhibited a range of association strengths with AVR-PikD.
source: The western blot analysis revealed that the ancHMA variants exhibited a range of association strengths with AVR-PikD (Figure 3B; Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Based on co-IP experiments shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: In every case, the association with ancHMA proteins was weaker than with the present-day Pikp-HMA.
source: In every case, the association with ancHMA proteins was weaker than with the present-day Pikp-HMA, indicating that binding strength has likely changed over the course of the Pikp-HMA evolutionary history.
evidence: Based on co-IP experiments comparing ancHMA and Pikp-HMA binding to AVR-PikD.

claim: Binding strength between HMA and AVR-PikD has likely changed over the course of the Pikp-HMA evolutionary history.
source: In every case, the association with ancHMA proteins was weaker than with the present-day Pikp-HMA, indicating that binding strength has likely changed over the course of the Pikp-HMA evolutionary history.
evidence: Inference drawn from comparison of ancestral and modern HMA binding to AVR-PikD.

claim: Only the Pikp-1:ancHMALVKIE chimera associated with the effector at levels similar to Pikp-1.
source: Among tested constructs, only the Pikp-1:ancHMALVKIE chimera associated with the effector at levels similar to Pikp-1 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on co-IP experiments shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The polymorphic residues in the IAQVV/LVKIE region are critical for the evolution of enhanced AVR-PikD binding in Pikp-1.
source: This indicates that the polymorphic residues in the IAQVV/LVKIE region are critical for the evolution of enhanced AVR-PikD binding in Pikp-1.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from chimera swap experiments showing only LVKIE region confers binding.

claim: AncHMALVKIE formed the strongest interaction with AVR-PikD at levels similar to Pikp-HMA.
source: AncHMALVKIE formed the strongest interaction with AVR-PikD at levels similar to Pikp-HMA, followed by ancHMALAKIE, then ancHMALAQVV, ancHMALAKIV, and ancHMA, which showed weaker interactions; we did not record any significant binding for ancHMALAKVV (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 4B; Supplementary file 1I).
evidence: Based on SPR experiments shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The two most recent mutations, Ala-222-Val and Val-230-Glu (AV-VE), collectively determined HMA transition towards high-affinity AVR-PikD binding.
source: These results indicate that the two most recent mutations, Ala-222-Val and Val-230-Glu, collectively referred to as AV-VE, determined HMA transition towards high-affinity AVR-PikD binding.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from SPR experiments showing binding hierarchy of mutants.

claim: The AV-VE polymorphisms are unique to Pikp-1 and Pikh-1 of rice.
source: We noted from the panel of 19 integrated HMA sequences collected in this study that the AV-VE polymorphisms are unique to Pikp-1 and Pikh-1 of rice.
evidence: Based on examination of HMA sequences from 19 integrated HMAs.

claim: Pikp-1 and Pikh-1 are highly similar to each other; out of a total of three polymorphisms, there is only one synonymous substitution that distinguishes their nearly 3500-bp-long coding sequences.
source: The Pikp-1 and Pikh-1 genes are highly similar to each other; out of a total of three polymorphisms, there is only one synonymous substitution that distinguishes their nearly 3500-bp-long coding sequences (Supplementary file 1J).
evidence: Based on sequence comparison of Pikp-1 and Pikh-1.

claim: The near-absence of synonymous nucleotide polymorphisms between Pikp-1 and Pikh-1 suggests a very recent emergence of the AV-VE polymorphisms.
source: Although this precludes a rigorous estimation of evolutionary divergence times of the integrated HMAs, the near-absence of synonymous nucleotide polymorphisms between Pikp-1 and Pikh-1 suggests a very recent emergence of the AV-VE polymorphisms.
evidence: Inference drawn from low synonymous substitution rate between Pikp-1 and Pikh-1.

claim: The AV-VE substitutions are sufficient to increase binding affinity towards the AVR-PikD effector independently of the other three polymorphic residues in the IAQVV/LVKIE interface.
source: These results indicate that the AV-VE substitutions are sufficient to increase binding affinity towards the AVR-PikD effector independently of the other three polymorphic residues in this IAQVV/LVKIE interface.
evidence: Based on co-IP experiments with ancHMAIVQVE mutant.

claim: All Pikp-1:ancHMA variants are autoactive and trigger spontaneous cell death in the absence of the effector.
source: We discovered that all Pikp-1:ancHMA variants are autoactive and trigger spontaneous cell death in the absence of the effector (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Based on HR cell death assays shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and 2.

claim: The presence of the Pikp-2 partner is required for Pikp-1:ancHMA autoactivity.
source: Notably, the presence of the Pikp-2 partner is required for Pikp-1:ancHMA autoactivity.
evidence: Based on HR cell death assays requiring co-expression with Pikp-2.

claim: The PMASDKH/AMEGNND region, located in the β1–α1 and α2–β4 loops of the Pikp-HMA domain, underpins Pikp-1:ancHMA autoactivity.
source: These results suggest that the PMASDKH/AMEGNND region, located in the β1–α1 and α2–β4 loops of the Pikp-HMA domain, underpins Pikp-1:ancHMA autoactivity.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from chimera experiments showing loss of autoactivity with AMEGNND mutations.

claim: The strength of binding directly correlates with the strength of HR.
source: Co-expression with AVR-PikD revealed that the strength of binding directly correlates with the strength of HR.
evidence: Based on comparison of binding affinity and HR phenotypes across mutants.

claim: The Pikp-1:ancHMALVKIE* mutant triggered cell death at levels similar to Pikp-1.
source: The Pikp-1:ancHMALVKIE* mutants triggered cell death at levels similar to Pikp-1, whereas the HR triggered by Pikp-1:ancHMALAKIE* was slightly, yet significantly, reduced when compared to Pikp-1.
evidence: Based on HR cell death assays shown in Figure 6B, C.

claim: The HR triggered by Pikp-1:ancHMALAKIE* was slightly, yet significantly, reduced when compared to Pikp-1.
source: The Pikp-1:ancHMALVKIE* mutants triggered cell death at levels similar to Pikp-1, whereas the HR triggered by Pikp-1:ancHMALAKIE* was slightly, yet significantly, reduced when compared to Pikp-1.
evidence: Based on HR cell death assays shown in Figure 6B, C.

claim: Pikp-1:ancHMA*, Pikp-1:ancHMALAKVV*, and Pikp-1:ancHMALAQVV* did not elicit cell death above background levels.
source: By contrast, Pikp-1:ancHMA*, Pikp-1:ancHMALAKVV*, and Pikp-1:ancHMALAQVV* did not elicit cell death above background levels.
evidence: Based on HR cell death assays shown in Figure 6B, C.

claim: The adaptive mutations in the IAQVV/LVKIE region towards AVR-PikD binding at high affinity also enable effector-dependent activation of the cell death immune response.
source: Overall, these results indicate that the adaptive mutations in the IAQVV/LVKIE region towards AVR-PikD binding at high affinity also enable effector-dependent activation of the cell death immune response.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from correlation between binding affinity and HR phenotypes.

claim: Only the Pikm-1:ancHMAEMVKE chimera associated with AVR-PikD among the five chimeras tested.
source: Among the five chimeras tested in this experiment, Pikm-1:ancHMAEMVKE was the only one to associate with AVR-PikD (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Based on co-IP experiments shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pikm-HMA evolved towards association with AVR-PikD through mutations in the MKANK/EMVKE region, a distinct interface from the IAQVV/LVKIE region of Pikp-1.
source: Overall, we conclude that Pikm-HMA evolved towards association with AVR-PikD through mutations in the MKANK/EMVKE region, a distinct interface from the IAQVV/LVKIE region of Pikp-1.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from chimera experiments showing EMVKE region confers binding in Pikm-1.

claim: Among tested mutants the ancHMAEMVKE displayed the highest rates of interaction with AVR-PikD, followed by ancHMAEMANK and ancHMAMKANK.
source: Accounting for this stoichiometry, we carried out SPR experiments using the same experimental design as in the Pikp-HMA assays and discovered that among tested mutants the ancHMAEMVKE displayed the highest rates of interaction with AVR-PikD, followed by ancHMAEMANK and ancHMAMKANK.
evidence: Based on SPR experiments shown in Figure 8C, D.

claim: The ANK-VKE substitutions are essential for Pikm-HMA high-affinity binding of AVR-PikD.
source: These findings indicate that the ANK-VKE substitutions are essential for Pikm-HMA high-affinity binding of AVR-PikD.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from SPR experiments showing binding hierarchy of mutants.

claim: The ANK-VKE substitutions are present in three Pik-1 alleles of rice, namely closely related Pik*-1, Pikm-1, and Piks-1.
source: We further noted that the ANK-VKE substitutions are present in three Pik-1 alleles of rice, namely closely related Pik*-1 (Zhai et al., 2011), Pikm-1 (Ashikawa et al., 2008), and Piks-1 (Jia et al., 2009; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on sequence comparison shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and cited literature.

claim: Pikm-1 differs from Piks-1 and Pik*-1 by only two and eight amino acid polymorphisms, respectively, but no synonymous changes.
source: Pikm-1 differs from Piks-1 and Pik*-1 by only two and eight amino acid polymorphisms, respectively, but no synonymous changes (Supplementary file 1J).
evidence: Based on sequence comparison of Pikm-1, Piks-1, and Pik*-1.

claim: The lack of synonymous changes demonstrates a very recent emergence of these Pik-1 alleles and their associated ANK-VKE substitutions.
source: This demonstrates a very recent emergence of these Pik-1 alleles and their associated ANK-VKE substitutions.
evidence: Inference drawn from absence of synonymous substitutions between closely related alleles.

claim: The MKANK/EMVKE and IAQVV/LVKIE regions map to two of the three interaction interfaces previously described to underpin binding of AVR-PikD, and other AVR-Pik variants, to Pik-HMAs.
source: We note that the MKANK/EMVKE and IAQVV/LVKIE regions map to two of the three interaction interfaces previously described to underpin binding of AVR-PikD, and other AVR-Pik variants, to Pik-HMAs (De la Concepcion et al., 2021; De la Concepcion et al., 2019; De la Concepcion et al., 2018).
evidence: Based on structural analysis and cited literature on AVR-Pik binding interfaces.

claim: The Val-230-Glu (V230E) substitution enhances the interaction with AVR-PikD through hydrogen bond formation with His-46.
source: Close inspection of these structures revealed that the Val-230-Glu (V230E) substitution enhances the interaction with AVR-PikD through hydrogen bond formation with His-46 (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Based on structural analysis shown in Figure 9A and Figure 9—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In both Pikm-HMA and Pikp-HMA, Lys-262 (K262) is a major effector-binding determinant that forms hydrogen bonds or salt bridges with Glu-53 and Ser-72 of AVR-PikD.
source: In both cases, Lys-262 (K262) is a major effector-binding determinant that forms hydrogen bonds or salt bridges with Glu-53 and Ser-72 of AVR-PikD (Figure 9A).
evidence: Based on structural analysis shown in Figure 9A.

claim: In Pikm-HMA the position of Lys-262 (K262) is structurally shifted causing a difference in the conformation of the HMA peptide backbone, and associated side chains, compared to Pikp-HMA.
source: However, in Pikm-HMA the position of Lys-262 (K262) is structurally shifted causing a difference in the conformation of the HMA peptide backbone, and associated side chains, compared to Pikp-HMA.
evidence: Based on structural comparison of Pikm-HMA and Pikp-HMA.

claim: Asn-262-Lys (N262K) and Lys-263-Glu (K263E) of the ANK-VKE substitution likely determine differential binding between the ancestral and present-day Pikm-HMA domains.
source: We conclude that Asn-262-Lys (N262K) and Lys-263-Glu (K263E) of the ANK-VKE substitution likely determine differential binding between the ancestral and present-day Pikm-HMA domains.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from structural analysis and binding experiments.
